# Separate XYZ

Splits a position or direction into its X, Y and Z values.

`lfs.separate_xyz` · Utilities

## How to use

Connect Position, then send the height axis to Compare or Map Range.  
Check which axis points up in your scene.  

## Inputs

| Name | Identifier | Type | Default | Range / choices | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Vector | `Vector` | lfs.vector | [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] | step 0.01; accepts per-element values | X, Y and Z values in the units you need. The default (0, 0, 0) gives zero on every axis. |

## Outputs

| Name | Identifier | Type | Default | Range / choices | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| X | `X` | lfs.float | — | — | X coordinate of the input, in the same units. 0 lies on the other two axes' plane. |
| Y | `Y` | lfs.float | — | — | Y coordinate of the input, in the same units. 0 lies on the other two axes' plane. |
| Z | `Z` | lfs.float | — | — | Z coordinate of the input, in the same units. 0 lies on the other two axes' plane. |
